newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Dlr/yen vols continue to creep lower.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Dlr/yen vols continue to creep lower.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar-yen options continued their gradual descent Thursday as spot dollar stayed glued to familiar levels.

One-month dollar/yen volatility slipped to 9.60/9.85 percent from 9.80/10.10 at Wednesday's close, with two-month at 9.75/9.90, down from 9.90/10.10, six-month at 10.15/10.35, down from 10.30/10.50 and one-year at 10.35/10.45, down from 10.45/10.50.
The effects would be felt particularly for options with one- and two-month durations, steepening the curve, he said.

On the other hand, "if something happens to make the spot market move out of its familiar range, volatility could jump much higher and the yield curve flatten at higher levels," the options analyst said.

Some speculative investors, anticipating dollar-bearish comments from Rubin, were buying dollar put/yen call positions in short-dated options, traders said. Countering that trend are Japanese investors who are bullish on the dollar long term and are buying dollar calls in 124, 125 and 126 strikes.
"Fresh buying interest in the new fiscal year has been very strong from Japanese institutions," said the Japanese bank analyst.

Dollar/mark volatilities, which have slumped to even lower levels across the curve than dollar/yen, were mostly steady Thursday as traders appeared unwilling to push them lower still, market participants said.
One-month dollar/mark was quoted at 9.00/9.30 percent, two-month at 9.15/9.35, six-month at 9.45/9.60 and one-year at 9.50/9.65.
With sentiment in dollar/mark growing increasingly bearish, few investors appear willing to buy puts or calls until spot market direction becomes clearer, traders said.
Risk reversals for dollar/mark reflect the bearish mood, at 0.1/0.2 in favor of mark calls for one-month 25-delta options.
Risk reversals in dollar/yen remain skewed toward yen puts at flat/0.15.
